title: Treaty of the Pyrenees
summary: The Treaty of the Pyrenees, signed on 7 November 1659 on Pheasant Island in the Bidasoa River, ended a 24-year war between France and Spain. France gained Roussillon and Artois, and the treaty arranged the marriage of Louis XIV to the Spanish infanta Marie-Thérèse.

uncertainty.note: Ministers signed on 7 November 1659; EBSCO says the two monarchs met to sign on 6 June 1660.

where.modern_name: Pheasant Island, Bidasoa River, between Hendaye (France) and Irun (Spain)
where.historical_name: Île des Faisans (Isle of Pheasants), Bidasoa River on the France–Spain border

importance.justification: Ended the long Franco-Spanish war, shifted territory to France and signalled a change in the balance of power in Europe.

sources.title: Île des Faisans, sur la Bidassoa (Hendaye, France et Irun, Espagne) – Traité des Pyrénées, 1659
sources.publisher: Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (France)

reviewer_note: Pin is Pheasant Island (signing site) from Atlas Obscura coordinates. EBSCO also gives 6 June 1660 as the monarchs' signing meeting; 7 Nov 1659 used as the treaty date.
